diagnosis: The check C3 passed in all four rollouts because the decision-maker set the initial rollout percentage to 5%, which triggers C3 due to the low percentage. This value is easily hit by generic caution or fairness, making the check unnecessary given the hidden information. The fact PF1, which changes the plan from ordinary cache enablement to either enabling the adapter or recording a binding commitment, is not accessed by the decision-maker in any of the rollouts, thus leaking the solution to C3.

C3.why: The passing tests do not expose the 23 legacy endpoints, and PF1 changes the plan from ordinary cache enablement to either enabling the adapter or recording a binding commitment to build and verify it before expanding the rollout.
